results.hypothesis: To determine whether incorporating Fama-French three-factor returns (Mkt-RF, SMB, HML) as auxiliary prediction targets in a multi-task learning model for credit default prediction improves out-of-sample AUC performance compared to a single-task model trained only on borrower-level features.
results.author: coder-agent
results.baseline: Single-task model trained only on borrower-level features without auxiliary macroeconomic targets
results.success_criteria: If the multi-task model achieves higher AUC than the single-task model on out-of-sample test data, the hypothesis is supported. If the AUC is equal or lower, the hypothesis is refuted.
results.notes: Multi-task model achieved AUC of 0.8324. To determine if this supports the hypothesis, a single-task model would need to be trained and compared.

reference_implementations.title: Towards Understanding Generalization of Macro-AUC in Multi-label Learning
reference_implementations.tldr: Theoretical analysis of different learning algorithms for Macro-AUC reveals that label-wise class imbalance critically affects generalization, with univariate loss-based algorithms being more sensitive than pairwise and reweighted loss-based ones.

reference_implementations.title: Curriculum-based Asymmetric Multi-task Reinforcement Learning
reference_implementations.tldr: CAMRL, a curriculum-based asymmetric multi-task learning algorithm, improves performance across various reinforcement learning tasks by dynamically adjusting training modes and optimizing a composite loss function.
